_provenance_note: Counts below are transcribed directly from Section 8.1 of the Academic Writing Engine Master Build Handoff (7 Aug 2026), which itself states the numbers come from the saved Davis Academic Language Corpus v0.1 analytical baseline (v0.9). No narrower cell (e.g. a specific region+degree+discipline+section combination) has an independently computed count yet -- that requires the Phase 2 ingestion/coverage-density pipeline described in Section 10.1. Until that exists, only these two broad families are marked 'supported'; every narrower request falls back to one of them.

features.cadence: Wide historical range; batch-level average sentence lengths from roughly 18 to almost 30 words. Do not enforce a single threshold as an authorship signal.
features.cohesion: Explicit transition frequency varies widely across credible sources, from sparse to frequent. Do not globally ban or globally require transition words.
features.researcher_presence: First-person singular, first-person plural, and impersonal/study-centred voice are all attested in credible sources. Do not auto-convert pronoun usage.
features.epistemic_stance: Credible sources show explicit hedging, qualification, and visible disagreement with prior literature rather than smoothing it away.
features.citation_integration: Numeric results are frequently interpreted in ordinary prose immediately after being reported; narrative and parenthetical citation styles both occur.
features.lexical_register: Technical/discipline terminology is repeated for precision rather than varied for its own sake.
features.grammar_tolerance: High polish and ordinary grammatical/collocational unevenness coexist in credible historical dissertations. Never inject errors to simulate humanity; never treat perfect grammar as proof of AI authorship.

features.cadence: Doctoral-length prose; some historical dissertations have over a third of screened sentences at 30+ words. Long sentences are not automatically AI-flavoured; short sentences are not automatically human.
features.cohesion: Content-led cohesion (subject continuity, logical progression) is at least as common as explicit transition markers in strong discussion sections.
features.researcher_presence: Frequent first-person empirical reporting ("I"/"we") is legitimate and replicated across multiple independent quantitative dissertations in the corpus.
features.epistemic_stance: Strong discussion sections connect result -> prior literature -> interpretation/boundary condition; limitations name actual measures, samples, estimators or settings rather than generic caveats.
features.citation_integration: Citation-to-claim relationships are close and specific; avoid moving a cited claim away from its supporting citation during restructuring.
features.lexical_register: Discipline-specific terminology (accounting/finance concentration is currently strongest) repeats deliberately; resist gratuitous synonym replacement of technical terms.
features.grammar_tolerance: Same as global default -- polish varies; do not manufacture errors or treat flawless grammar as suspicious.
